statement: The U.S. Department of Justice announced on October 1, 2026 the arrest of a California man on a three-count indictment alleging his company bought and smuggled more than 300 million dollars of export-controlled high-end servers containing U.S.-made graphics processors to China between 2023 and 2024, including one purchase order for 27 servers worth 7.6 million dollars.
why: A criminal case of this size shows both that unauthorised Chinese demand for top-end accelerators is large and that U.S. enforcement is actively closing those channels, which cuts the market the vendor can legally serve.

impact.mechanism: Active prosecution of diversion channels removes gray-market volume and raises compliance burdens on resellers and server makers, shrinking legally addressable accelerator demand even as it evidences strong unmet Chinese appetite.

evidence.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
evidence.excerpt: more than $300 million worth of export-controlled high-end computer servers

evidence.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The National Security Division will protect the American advantage in the chips that power this technology.

confidence.basis: Government press release, but the figures are untested indictment allegations and the chipmaker is not named as a party.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
entity: Earthmade Computer Inc. / Greg Lui / China
